newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian rebels said to plan stepped up attacks.
newsitem.headline: Colombian rebels said to plan stepped up attacks.

text.p: Colombia's leftist rebels plan to step up their long-running guerrilla war and move from the countryside to the cities to force the government into peace talks, a government official said on Thursday.

Jose Fernando Castro, the government's "public defender" or human rights ombudsman, spoke of the rebel strategy in an interview with local radio after holding several hours of talks with Francisco Galan, a jailed leader of the National Liberation Army (ELN).
"The guerrillas...see the conflict and the war intensifying, they're going to carry it into the cities," Castro said.
"This means that we have to start thinking seriously about a process of dialogue," he said. "Because if we don't, we're going to have another 140 years of bloodshed in Colombia."
Castro did not make it clear in his comments to Radionet if his reading of the rebel strategy was based entirely on his discussion with Galan, the No. 3 leader of the ELN.
But army commander Gen. Manuel Jose Bonett said recently that he expected to see increased rebel activity in rural and urban areas alike.

Castro said the ELN and the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), the country's largest rebel group, were both planning to launch offensives aimed at bringing the government to the bargaining table.

Galan is allowed to keep a radio telephone in his cell in Bogota's Modelo prison and is said to remain in close touch with other leaders of the group founded by radical Roman Catholic priests in the mid-1960s.
He has been locked up since 1992 but is still considered one of the country's most influential guerrilla leaders.
